label: FP
reason: User input from HTTP header is URL-decoded, passed through doSomething() which invokes ThingFactory.createThing().doSomething(), then encrypted with AES/CCM cipher. The encrypted bytes are converted to String and HTML-encoded via ESAPI.encodeForHTML() before printing to response. Encryption fundamentally transforms arbitrary input into random-looking bytes, destroying any XSS payload semantics. The HTML encoding provides defense-in-depth by escaping special characters. The reported XSS sink is therefore mitigated.

evidence.note: User input flows through header→URL decode→doSomething()→encryption→String conversion→HTML encoding→response print
